_levels: 2.66.0 (Aleksis: no flexibility otherwise): a finding BLOCKS the build only for a clear physical error - a thing the words name drawn nowhere (no kin part either: 'kin' lists what may stand for it, a hose drawn as a pipe), a deck part inside the hull, a pipe end far from everything, a spray or curtain far from everything, a step that says the gas vents with none leaving, a row of named captions over nothing, a mode caption over no engine. Everything else is a NOTE the figure reviewer judges. A spec accepts a finding on purpose with "meaning_ok": {"<KIND> <part id>": "<why it is right>"}.
_what: What a figure MEANS - read by course-visuals/kit/scripts/kit_meaning.py (check_kit.py spec, every build) and by the workflow's FIGURE review (2.66.0). 'names': words that name a thing, and the kit parts that draw it - words on a figure (a text part, a part's label) or in a step's title naming a thing the figure does not draw is a build FAIL. 'figures': the common IGF pictures and what must be true in each; a figure is of a kind when its words match 'when' (and it has the parts in 'needs_one_of', when given). Each 'truth' is a rule id kit_meaning.py knows, and 'says' is the sentence a builder and a reviewer read. Source: IGF Code (MSC.391(95)) and the IGF Basic hand-fixed course (Drosibas pamatkurss, 2026-10).

deck_mounted._what: parts that stand on or above the open deck of a side-view ship (ga): never inside the hull

ship_plan.title: Ship general arrangement with the IGF spaces

truths.says: every vent mast stands on the open deck and its outlet is clearly above the deck (and above the accommodation when one is drawn) - never inside the hull
the bunkering station (manifold, coupling), a hatch and an air intake sit on or above the open deck
a fuel tank in a hold is inside the hull, below the deck
the tank connection space sits on the tank (at its top or end), touching it
every space or item the words name is drawn - a bunkering station is a manifold on deck, not a word

ship_plan.source: IGF Basic M01 s04 (hand-fixed), IGF Code 5.3 / 6.7 / 8.3

bunkering_line.title: Bunkering line at the bunkering station

truths.says: the hose, coupling, valves and manifold form one connected line - every pipe and hose end meets a part
a drip tray is under the coupling / manifold flange, where a leak drips
a water curtain hangs from the deck edge down the ship's side under the bunkering station - attached, not floating
every valve, coupling and tray the words name is drawn

bunkering_line.source: IGF Basic M03 s15 / s16, M07 s14, M13 s09 (hand-fixed); IGF Code 8.3, 8.4

vent_system.title: Vent system: tank, relief valve, vent mast, gas out

truths.says: the vent mast is connected by its pipe to the relief valve (and the relief valve to the tank)
a step shows the gas leaving the vent outlet (puffs or a cloud from the outlet), the step the relief valve lifts
the vent outlet is the highest point of the gas path - the gas leaves upwards, into free air
with a ship drawn, the vent outlet is above the deck

vent_system.source: IGF Basic M03 s09, M15 s05 (hand-fixed); IGF Code 6.7

fuel_supply.title: Fuel supply: tank, TCS, FPR, master valve, engine

truths.says: one connected pipe path runs from the tank to the engine
the master valve (and any valve the words name) sits on that path, outside the engine room
every item on the path the words name (vaporizer, pump, gas valve unit) is drawn on the path

fuel_supply.source: IGF Basic M02 s03 / s04 / s05 (hand-fixed); IGF Code 9.4

truths.says: each mode named as a caption heads its own drawing of the engine or cylinder in that mode (or the modes are steps of one drawing) - no caption over nothing, no caption over a different part
the injectors and valves the words name are drawn

fuel_types.title: Fuel types

truths.says: each fuel named in the grid has its own drawing (its tank, its bar or its place on a scale) - never one tank and five words

fuel_types.source: IGF Basic M01 s02 (hand-fixed: one scale, every fuel on it)
